Rider and driver: this dispute is decided on the record, without a human reviewer.

Outcome. The $4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider stands and is not refunded, and the driver is paid $3.60 compensation.

(b) The exported GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at that moment: 41 fixes qualify, the closest 0.16 m from the pin, well beyond the three consecutive accuracy-filtered in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires. (c) He held position in one continuous run of 400 seconds, from 18:06:05 to 18:12:45, against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) — a surplus of 220 seconds. (d) He terminated the trip at 18:12:48 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event, which is after the required dwell elapsed. The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: at 18:06:05 the driver was 0.16 m from the pin and stationary, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or above, so the waiting clock legitimately runs from that fix.

What each side argued. The rider is right that POL-NS-12 cannot assist the driver here — this trip's arrival marker is a driver-pressed BUTTON, and POL-NS-12 covers only GPS_AUTO arrivals. That point is accepted but immaterial, because the POL-NS-02 geofence test is satisfied on the exported trace itself. The rider is also right that POL-NS-06 does not open: 400 seconds is a surplus against the 180-second minimum, not a shortfall, so no refund flows from premature cancellation. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the only message in the chat log is the driver's, sent 18:06:25, so the rider sent no locating or coordinating message and limb (a) fails. POL-NS-03 does not apply either — the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m — so this is not a wrong-entrance case. The driver's alternative reference to the 300-second fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec does not govern a record that carries platform_policy, as this one does; the governing minimum is 180 seconds, and 400 seconds clears either figure.

Rider's own position. The rider's device recorded 71 stationary fixes averaging about 788 m from the pin, outside the 100 m rider-presence radius. That reading is not disputed and is not used against the rider: the rider's distance is not an element of the charge, which turns on the driver's arrival, dwell and cancellation. It simply means POL-NS-04 cannot help him.

The missing traffic advisory. EV-ADVIS-02745-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and, under POL-GEN-02, can carry no fact; the absence is itself noted. It is not needed here: the driver's 400-second hold was one unbroken run, so no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is required.

Driver's pay. The anti-farming check does not trip: one no-show termination in the trailing 30 days (below 4) at a rate of 0.008 (below 0.08), and both limbs must hold. The ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same $3.60 as the compensation figure; the rider's own $4.50 charge is unaffected and the two are not netted.

If that test is not satisfied on the trace as the judge runs it, POL-NS-02 entitles the rider to a full refund of the $4.50 cancellation fee.

The rider's one arithmetic route to a refund, the POL-NS-06 shortfall, does not open on this record and the rider does not contend otherwise: the free waiting period in force is 180 s (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, which governs because this record carries platform_policy, not the pre-version-2 zone table), and the derived longest qualifying in-geofence run is 400 s of continuous holding from 18:06:05 to 18:12:45 - a surplus of 220 s, not a shortfall. The rider puts the point no higher than this: only time actually held inside the 50 m arrival radius counts, and time spent outside that radius, or in motion, cannot be added to the 180 s.

The rider does not press POL-NS-04 and does not claim it exonerates him: the chat log holds one message, the driver's ('im at the pickup point', sent 18:06:25, read by the rider at 18:06:55, and carrying no waypoint_hint), the rider sent no locating message of his own and no in-app call was placed, so limb (a) is not met. The rider's silence is not, however, a finding against him, and it does not relieve the driver of proving every limb of POL-NS-01: POL-NS-04 is a rider-exonerating route, and its non-satisfaction is not an element of the charge.

The driver cannot accumulate waiting time across separate in-geofence intervals: EV-ADVIS-02745-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; admissibility weight 0.0, and the rider discloses that impairment) and POL-NS-06(i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, of an admissible type (KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT), before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed - so no advisory on this record can extend the measured dwell beyond the single run the trace shows, and no part of the waiting time can be rescued by limb (i).

The rider's own device recorded 71 stationary fixes averaging 788 m from the pickup pin, and the rider does not dispute that reading - but the rider's distance from the pin is not an element of the charge: POL-NS-01 conditions the fee on the driver's in-geofence dwell, the driver's arrival and the driver's cancellation under a recognised reason code, not on proof that the rider was absent, so the rider's track neither adds to the driver's case nor supplies a fact the driver's own evidence must establish.

The trip record carries the driver's own 'arrived' event for this trip at 18:06:05 on 2026-08-17 ('Driver tapped I'm Here', PLATFORM_TELEMETRY), which satisfies POL-NS-01(a) on the face of the record.

The driver held position inside the geofence in one continuous run of 41 fixes lasting 400 seconds, from 18:06:05 to 18:12:45. That wrong-entrance route applies only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; here the stationary fixes lie inside the radius (minimum distance 0.157 m, all 41 qualifying fixes in-radius), so this is not a wrong-face-of-the-venue case and no refund flows from it.
